note: The why says what makes the drill pay off (a moved chord is named by the note under it), each block is the same game turned a new way (find, name, every place), and every step says what to press, who acts (the game) and how the answer is given: by playing into the mic, by a name button, by tapping the neck. Done is a feel (no counting frets), never a count.

exercise.title: Notes on the low E and A strings
exercise.focus: Natural notes on the E and A strings · frets 0 to 12 · find, name, every place
exercise.why: A chord shape moved up the neck is named by the note under it on the low E or the A string, so knowing these notes lets you find any chord you move.

sections.text: Under the neck below, press Playing it (mic), then press Start above the neck. The game names a note: find it on the low E or the A string and play it, saying its name out loud. Keep going until you stop counting frets from the open string.

Press Start in the game below. Now the game lights a note on the neck: press its name under the neck. Play the note on your guitar as you answer, so your hand learns the place while your eyes learn the name.

Press Start in the game below. The game names a note: tap every place it sits on the two strings, then play those places on your guitar, low to high. Now make up your own round: pick any note and find it on both strings.
